source.question: e-9035
source.value:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} = \ln(x + y).
$$

Using a substitution of the form $z= x + y,$ transform the differential equation into an equation of the form $z'(x) = f(z).$ What is the function $f(z)?$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-9035

source.question: e-9035
source.value:
First, we make the substitution

$$
z = x + y.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x}  = 1 + \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x} - 1.
$$

Therefore, the original equation can be written in terms of $z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡z\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing this equation in the form $z'(x) = f(z),$ we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x}  = \ln z+1.
$$

Therefore, $f(z) = \ln z + 1.$

decisions.question: e-9037

source.question: e-9037
source.value:
First, we make the substitution

$$
z = x+y.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x}  = 1 + \,\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x} - 1.
$$

Therefore, the original equation can be written in terms of $z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-1 & =z\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing this equation in the form $z'(x) = f(z)$ gives

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x}  = z+1.
$$

This differential equation is separable. So, we separate the variables and integrate both sides with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{z+1}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =1 \\ \int \frac{1}{z+1}\,\text{d}z & =\int \,\text{d}x \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|z+1| & =x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the equation in terms of $y$ and $x$ using our original substitution, as follows:

$$
\ln{|x+y+1|}  = x + C
$$

Therefore, $g(x,y) = \ln{|x+y+1|}.$
